label: Kimi K3.1 Pro
output:
Sizwe, breathe, chief. Congratulations on tomorrow. Now **take the key out and don’t crank it again — not even one “last try”.** Every turn runs the pump on petrol with no lubrication.

Kobus means well, but that’s old Land Rover advice. Your 2019 common-rail D-Max can’t take it. And don’t pour diesel on top: the petrol is still in there. Mixing it with more fuel does absolutely nothing except give you a fuller tank of the wrong stuff.

You drove it until it stalled and cranked it repeatedly, so damage is possible. I won’t lie to you. But **R40 000 is not a diagnosis**, especially not from someone sitting next to it in the dark. Tow it — don’t drive it — and have the pump and injectors inspected first. If they’re okay, it’s drain the tank, flush the lines, new fuel filter and bleed the system. That’s usually around **R2 500–R4 500**. I can’t promise you a final total tonight until we’ve seen what damage, if any, has been done.

Check your insurance policy now for roadside towing before paying a tow oke cash. My shop is in **Umbilo**, open **Saturday 7 till 12**. Get it to us and Thabo can start draining it first thing once we know what we’re dealing with.

And borrow a bakkie for tomorrow **anyway**, for the cake and sound system. Don’t plan your wedding around whether we finish bleeding a fuel system. The cake does not need to attend a diagnostic.

You’re not the first oke beaten by a fuel nozzle. One customer did it twice in the same year, at the same garage. We made him a sticker for the inside of his fuel flap. In my first apprentice year, 1995, I put diesel in the boss’s Golf. He still tells that story at every braai, so you’ve got years of material here.

Key out. Arrange the tow and a loan bakkie, then go get some sleep. We’ll worry about the D-Max; you’ve got a wedding to survive. Congrats again, man.
